title: Dormant parser bug activated by selective policy rollout
context: A regional authorization control-plane policy was rolled out at 09:10. The tenant_id is optional in the policy schema. Earlier parser releases incorrectly call .strip() on tenant_id without checking null, but only when a new policy is enabled. Regional stacks remain isolated except for the explicit dependency graph. All services and dependency edges are listed.
semantics: A policy-REGION locally crashes if rollout_enabled is true AND parser_version is strictly below 28 AND tenant_id is null or the empty/whitespace string. When rollout_enabled is false, the previous working snapshot remains active. A parser_version of 28 or higher correctly accepts a null tenant_id. Otherwise that policy node is healthy. This is the only local failure mechanism.

hypotheses.description: The US gateway has a missing tenant and therefore crashes.
The APAC gateway is unhealthy because its policy rollout is disabled.
The EU policy enables an older null-unsafe parser with a null tenant field.
All regions use a null-unsafe parser irrespective of version.

actions.meaning: Revert EU to its known-healthy prior policy snapshot
Set EU policy tenant_id to a nonblank valid identifier

provenance: Inspired by the general failure mechanism in the 2025-06-12 Google Cloud Service Control incident; facts and names are entirely fabricated.
